interpretation: Character-only already omits the vest, begins with an open top cover and does not perform the requested distinct post-smile flat-hand placement. These must not all be blamed on merging.

Additive, SLERP, TIES, stable winner and NP retain coarse short-curved-horn, broad-soft-muzzle features close to character-only. All five still omit the vest; none demonstrates a clear flat palm arriving after the smile. TIES and stable winner keep the book closed from the start; additive closes a raised cover, NP/SLERP set down a tilted book. These separate observations are not a composite quality score.

CT is the only merged arm retaining the vest, but differs visibly in face/horns, keeps exposed teeth, crops an upper horn and later moves a hand away from the book. It does not satisfy the combined identity/action/wardrobe requirement.

Base/effect-only also preserve the vest while depicting a long-horned, angular/bearded monster. Effect-only shows gaze-then-closed-mouth-smile and small later cover-edge placement; preserving those actions is not preserving the requested identity.

NP is close to additive in coarse character presentation, without a demonstrated identity advantage. Some gaze timing improves over the character-only clip, but not the complete requested sequence/wardrobe. No automatic method preference is justified.

interpretation: Base and character-only already show two long attempts plus an extra short far-side reach with uncertain contact. Effect-only has four attempts. Repetition is not exclusively a merge-induced fault.

All six merged arms show at least three attempted punches. Additive and SLERP each have five, stable winner and NP four, TIES and CT three; fewer attempts alone do not establish a better complete action or audiovisual result.

NP shows two far-near pairs, unlike additive's four far attempts followed by one near attempt, and has a settled lowered ending. That is a local ordering/count trade-off versus additive, not success at the requested single left-jab/right-straight pair and not a general NP preference.

TIES and CT have fewer attempts than additive but lower only late and do not reach a settled ending. Additive, SLERP, stable winner and NP lower earlier and hold the lowered pose. Anatomical left/right and hidden impact details remain inferential.

All merged arms retain a broadly similar long-haired facial presentation to character-only, with CT differing in darker/narrower-eyed presentation and hair drape. Hair, pose, expression and motion blur prevent a reliable fine-identity ordering. The creator's smiling close-up is not a pose-matched identity ground truth.
No merged arm satisfies exact count/order/guard/ending together. No audio identity or perceptual synchronization ranking can be inferred from the waveform groups.
